extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and their counsel, PTO/ OED disciplinary staff, administrative law judges
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural rules used to evaluate practitioner misconduct and to determine service, default, culpability, sanctions, and limited remedies in disciplinary proceedings before the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of complaint (37 C.F.R. § 11.35(a)(2) and § 11.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complaint in an OED disciplinary proceeding may be served on a respondent by express mail, first class mail, or any delivery service that provides the sender the ability to confirm 'delivery or attempted delivery' at the address the practitioner provided to the Office; service does not require the practitioner to accept delivery personally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence of delivery or attempted delivery (e.g., certified mail return receipts showing an agent's signature and 'Agent' box checked) satisfies the service requirement; mailing to the address provided to the PTO is sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to timely file answer equals admission/default (37 C.F.R. § 11.36(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to timely file an answer will constitute an admission of the allegations in the complaint and may result in entry of default judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer deadlines are counted from filing (e.g., 30 days); an unfiled answer supports a motion for default judgment and leads the tribunal to deem the Complaint's allegations admitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of default — admission of allegations and incorporation
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent's default constitutes an admission of each and every allegation in the Complaint; allegations and factual assertions in the Director's motion and exhibits may be incorporated into the Initial Decision by reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon default the tribunal can treat Complaint and supporting exhibits as the factual record for adjudicating violations and sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 10.23(a) — disreputable or gross misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in disreputable or gross misconduct is a violation of PTO Disciplinary Rule 10.23(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied where conduct by a practitioner demonstrates serious departure from professional norms; used as a basis for discipline including exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 10.23(b)(4) — dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation is proscribed under Rule 10.23(b)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes knowingly providing false information to clients or to OED (e.g., misrepresenting receipt type of a client's payment); such misrepresentations are material to discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 10.23(b)(5) — conduct prejudicial to administration of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice violates Rule 10.23(b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used where practitioner actions obstruct or undermine processes of the PTO or legal system (e.g., failure to respond to Office notices leading to abandonment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 10.23(b)(6) — conduct adversely reflecting on fitness to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct that adversely reflects on a practitioner's fitness to practice before the PTO violates Rule 10.23(b)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied where repeated or serious misconduct indicates lack of fitness (habitual neglect, misappropriation, deceit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 10.77(b) — handling a legal matter without adequate preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Handling a legal matter without preparation adequate in the circumstances is a violation of Rule 10.77(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers instances where lack of preparation results in missed deadlines, failure to file required fees, or other harms to client matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 10.77(c) — neglecting a legal matter entrusted to the practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: Neglecting a legal matter entrusted to the practitioner violates Rule 10.77(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to inform clients of Office notices, failing to respond to Office communications, or abandoning prosecution of applications are examples of neglect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 10.84(a)(1) — failing to seek clients' lawful objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to seek the lawful objectives of a client through reasonably available means permitted by law and the Disciplinary Rules violates Rule 10.84(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes not taking available actions to revive abandoned applications or otherwise protect clients' patent rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 10.84(a)(2) — failing to carry out contracts of employment with clients
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to carry out contracts of employment entered into with clients violates Rule 10.84(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: accepting advance fees to prepare/file/prosecute applications and then failing to perform or to refund unearned fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 10.89(c)(6) — intentional/habitual violation of Disciplinary Rules before a tribunal
rubrics_metrics.description: Intentionally and habitually violating PTO Disciplinary Rules in a professional capacity before a tribunal is proscribed under Rule 10.89(c)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports aggravated discipline where misconduct is repeated and intentional across multiple matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty considerations for sanctioning (37 C.F.R. § 11.54(b)(1)-(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining appropriate sanctions the tribunal must consider: (1) whether the practitioner violated a duty to client/public/legal system/profession; (2) whether the practitioner acted intentionally/knowingly/negligently; (3) the amount of actual or potential injury caused; and (4) existence of aggravating or mitigating factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These four factors are the controlling framework for deciding exclusion, suspension, or other discipline; each factor is weighed with the record (e.g., actual abandonment, financial harm, deliberate concealment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Available sanctions and limits on hearing officer's remedial authority (35 U.S.C. § 32; 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20(a), 11.54(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may impose exclusion, suspension, reprimand, censure, or probation; the hearing officer's initial decision is limited to an order of default judgment, suspension or exclusion from practice, reprimand, or dismissal of the complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Director can impose additional conditions in a final decision, the Initial Decision by the hearing officer is restricted to the enumerated remedies. The tribunal must follow these procedural limits when crafting initial orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and limits regarding restitution and conditions (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20(b), 11.56(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may require restitution to persons financially injured as a condition of probation or reinstatement, and may condition reinstatement on showing steps taken to correct or mitigate the conduct; the hearing officer's initial decision does not appear to include authority to order restitution or other conditions of probation/reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for restitution should be addressed to the Director's final decision stage; an Initial Decision must generally omit orders imposing restitution as a condition of reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform standards for PTO practitioners (37 C.F.R. § 10.20; 35 U.S.C. § 32)
rubrics_metrics.description: All PTO practitioners, whether agents or attorneys, are expected to meet the same standards of professional conduct and mandatory Disciplinary Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary expectations and sanctions apply equally to registered agents and attorneys practicing before the PTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seriousness of abandonment after accepting fees (ethical/evidentiary standard for sanction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Abandonment of a case or client after being paid for legal services is a significant ethical violation that has led to disbarment/exclusion in past cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple authorities and prior PTO decisions cited as precedent support exclusion for repeated abandonment, failure to return unearned fees, and failure to respond to investigations; habitual abandonment is an aggravating factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of disciplinary findings
rubrics_metrics.description: The facts and circumstances of disciplinary proceedings shall be fully published in the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office's official publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication is part of the disciplinary process and serves regulatory transparency and notice to the public and profession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-discipline duties and reinstatement procedures (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58, 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplined practitioners are subject to duties specified in § 11.58 and any petition for reinstatement must follow § 11.60 requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners excluded or suspended must comply with duties while disciplined and follow specified procedures and conditions when seeking reinstatement (including any conditions the Director imposes in a final decision).
